messages:
marta-peopleops: Hey @simon — congrats again! Quick checklist for your Germany (Berlin) start on May 15. Need to confirm a few visa/work-auth items so payroll and benefits can be set up.

simon-newhire: Thanks! I have the EU Blue Card approval PDF. Embassy is asking for an original employer letter showing salary in EUR and start date. Also worried about the Anmeldung — I’ll be in an Airbnb for the first week. Can payroll start without a registered address/Steuer-ID?

oliver-hr: We can generate the employer letter (signed + company letterhead). Payroll note: Steuer-ID is ideal but not strictly required to open payroll; however taxes/withholding may need adjustment once you have the ID. If you start before Anmeldung we might have to do a provisional payroll entry and reconcile later.

marta-peopleops: Action items for you, Simon: we need passport scan, the Blue Card approval pdf, and IBAN for payroll. On the employer letter: we can provide a notarized original and a certified German translation via our vendor. We can also provide an affidavit for the embassy if they accept hotel/temporary accommodation.

marta-peopleops: Quick doc checklist (we'll produce a downloadable packet):
```
- Passport bio page (scan)
- EU Blue Card approval letter (pdf)
- Signed employment contract (we have this)
- Employer letter on company letterhead (we'll generate)
- Proof of address for Anmeldung (landlord Wohnungsgeberbestätigung OR temporary hotel confirmation + employer affidavit for embassy)
- IBAN and tax residency form (W-8/other)
- Health insurance confirmation (Krankenkasse) — enroll within 2 weeks of arrival
```

simon-newhire: Embassy specifically asked for the employer letter to be in German or translated. Can you confirm translation + apostille? Also need the letter by May 1 for my appointment on May 3.

marta-peopleops: Yes — we will do a certified German translation and notarize the employer letter. For apostille: Germany accepts apostilles for US-issued documents; we'll route to GlobalDocs for apostille + translation. @globaldocs-bot will confirm turnaround.

globaldocs-bot: Received request token PR-45812. Estimated turnaround: 3 business days for notarize+translate, 5 business days if apostille required. We will notify when ready.

oliver-hr: Note to payroll: if Simon's start date is 2024-05-15 and Steuer-ID not present, payroll will process provisional net salary and correct once Steuer-ID arrives. There may be a one-time adjustment. I'll open a payroll ticket.

payroll-bot: Payroll ticket created: #PR-45812 — Owner: oliver-hr — Start date: 2024-05-15 — Notes: EU Blue Card onboarding, provisional payroll if no Steuer-ID.

simon-newhire: Timeline: visa stamping appointment May 3, arrive May 14. Can HR prepare the letter by end of day May 1? Also: for Anmeldung — if I use Airbnb first week, is a hotel confirmation + employer letter sufficient for the embassy?

marta-peopleops: We can get the draft ready by EOD May 1. For the embassy, hotel booking + employer affidavit typically works for the appointment; for Anmeldung after arrival you'll need the Wohnungsgeberbestätigung from your landlord. If you sign a short-term sublet/booking with a host, ask them for that form.

oliver-hr: I'll sign the letter once Marta posts the draft. Marta — please include salary in EUR, start date, reporting manager (Oliver), and a line confirming we will enroll them in statutory health insurance.

marta-peopleops: Will do. Drafting now, will DM for signatures. Simon — please upload passport + Blue Card pdf to: https://redwood-internal/hr-docs/upload?case=EU-BlueCard-1869991111 (secure link).

simon-newhire: Uploaded passport + Blue Card confirmation. Thanks all. One last Q: do I need to get any documents apostilled in the US before the appointment or can HR handle it from here?

marta-peopleops: HR will handle apostille and certified translation. We may ask you to sign a release form to send documents to GlobalDocs. I'll share the release and the draft letter in this thread by EOD. :thumbsup:
